claims.text: NiTi shape-memory alloys exhibit temperature-dependent plastic deformation behavior.
The temperature-dependent deformation behavior of NiTi is caused by a thermally driven martensitic transformation.
Lower temperatures shift NiTi toward more irreversible plastic deformation.
Higher temperatures produce largely reversible pseudoelastic behavior in NiTi.
The polycrystalline NiTi alloy is initially austenitic at room temperature.
Temperature variation across the martensitic-start temperature induces transformation between austenite and martensite.
The austenite-to-martensite transformation alters dislocation mobility and microstructural configuration.
Lower temperatures stabilize martensite in NiTi.
Martensite stabilization reduces the capacity for reversible deformation.
Martensite stabilization enhances dislocation activity and irreversible plasticity.
At higher temperatures, the austenitic phase favors recoverable pseudoelastic deformation.
Irreversible strain will be greater at lower temperatures than at higher temperatures.
Near the martensitic-start temperature, NiTi displays a balance between recoverable and plastic deformation.
The proposed temperature-dependent plastic-deformation behavior is unique to NiTi alloys having a well-defined martensitic transformation.
The proposed behavior might not apply to materials lacking a similar phase-transformation mechanism.
